name: Propane-precooled mixed refrigerant liquefaction (C3MR, AP-X)
principle: A propane refrigeration cycle precools the feed gas and the mixed refrigerant. A mixed refrigerant of nitrogen, methane, ethane and propane then liquefies and subcools the gas in a coil-wound main cryogenic heat exchanger. AP-X adds a nitrogen expander loop that subcools LNG from about -115 °C to about -150 °C, cutting mixed refrigerant flow by 40% per unit of LNG and allowing trains of 7.8 Mtpa and more.

performance.basis: design capacity of the six original Qatar AP-X trains and four North Field East trains; Air Products says trains can exceed 10 Mtpa

source.note: Air Products, LNG technology enables largest LNG trains (printed 2020)

performance.basis: NETL model of a US C3MR plant from Mallapragada et al. 2018; range covers adsorption or cryogenic heavy hydrocarbon removal, with or without HRSG; fuel is a parasitic stream of feed gas, not compressor shaft power

source.note: NETL, Life Cycle GHG Perspective on Exporting LNG from the United States: 2019 Update, DOE/NETL-2019/2041, 12 September 2019, Exhibits 5-7 and 5-11, Appendix B
